entries.description:
The BL-5C is a battery manufactured for Nokia phones. It was one of the most common Nokia batteries, produced from the debut of the 3650 in 2003 to 2022, when it was replaced with a pair of 1000 mAh batteries called the BL-L5E and BL-L5J.

Variants of this battery also existed, including:

BR-5C (970 mAh, produced ca. 2003-06) • rare nowadays, distinguishable by an inverted color scheme, included with the Nokia 2600
BL-5CA (700 mAh, ca. 2006-10) • included with certain low-end phones
BL-5CB (800 mAh, ca. 2010-22) • for certain low-end phones
BL-5CV (1050 mAh, ca. 2010) • for Vertu-branded phones
BL-L5G (800 mAh, 2022-date).

The BL-5C form factor was so popular that it was used as something of a de facto standard by unlicensed third parties for various other devices such as wireless keyboards, portable game consoles, small to medium form transistor radios and even Bluetooth speakers, likely due to its wide availability. Thanks to this, even following the end of the BL-5C's production run and long after the peak of BL-5C powered phones, brand new aftermarket replacements are still widely available for purchase.

Similar batteries:
Nokia BL-4C • same shape, but thinner, compatible
Nokia BL-5B • same shape, but shorter
Nokia BL-6C • same shape, but thicker, compatible

Recall:
On August 14th, 2007, Nokia has recalled 46 million BL-5C batteries worldwide due to batteries manufactured by Matsushita between December 2005 and November 2006 which could explode by a short circuit while charging. Nokia initiated a replacement program for the affected batteries.[2]

Source: Legacy Portable Computing Wiki contributors, https://lpcwiki.miraheze.org/wiki/Nokia_BL-5C (accessed 2026-09-24). CC BY-SA 4.0. Imported, structured and annotated; unknown values remain unknown.

The BML-3 is a battery manufactured for Nokia phones. It was only used on the Nokia 3210.

entries.name: BP-6M
entries.description:
The BP-6M is a battery used by some Nokia phones from the mid-2000s. It was introduced in 2004 with the Nokia 9300.

It came in two different revisions, as well as two different capacities (1070 mAh Li-ion / 1100 mAh Li-Po).

Similar batteries:
Nokia BP-6MT • Similar design, but incompatible due to different pinout
Nokia BP-5M • Same as BP-6MT, but slightly thinner

entries.name: BP-6MT
entries.description:
The BP-6MT is a battery manufactured for Nokia phones. It is a variant of the BP-6M with blade socket contacts, thus the two batteries are not cross compatible with each other.

Similar batteries:
Nokia BP-5M: Same size, slightly thinner, mostly interchangeable
Nokia BP-6M: Same shape and size, different pin style and pinout
Nokia BL-6Q: Same height and thickness, but narrower. A BL-6Q can be used with phones that use the BP-6MT (tested on the N82 and E51).

entries.name: LRW-1
entries.description:
The Nokia LRW-1 is a battery holder for a Nokia BLB-3 battery with a built-in Bluetooth module. It requires a Nokia 6210 phone with firmware 5.02 or a later version[1]. The Nokia LRW-1 is part of the Nokia Connectivity Pack, which was announced on 5 December 2000[2] additionally includes a Nokia DTL-1 CompactFlash Bluetooth card and a Nokia FLA-15 CompactFlash to PCMCIA adapter and a software CD-ROM containing drivers and a Bluetooth-enabled version of the Nokia PC Suite. It supports at least the Dial-up Networking profile[3].

Similar batteries:
Nokia BMS-2S • 900 mAh NiMH battery
Nokia BMS-2V • 900 mAh NiMH vibra battery
Nokia BLS-2N • 1050 mAh Li-ion battery
Nokia BLS-4 • 1500 mAh Li-ion extended battery
Nokia BPS-2 • 1100 mAh LiPo slim battery
Nokia BPS-1 • 600 mAh LiPo ultra slim battery

Source: Legacy Portable Computing Wiki contributors, https://lpcwiki.miraheze.org/wiki/Nokia_LRW-1 (accessed 2026-09-24). CC BY-SA 4.0. Imported, structured and annotated; unknown values remain unknown.
